role: New College Grad - Embedded Firmware Engineer
adjacent_skills: Lab equipment (oscilloscopes have, DMMs not explicit)
Board bring-up (PCB/EAGLE design experience is close but not explicit bring-up)
Firmware-electrical correlation (adjacent via PCB + bare-metal debug)
Signal integrity / power debugging (adjacent via Digital Signal Processing, Random Signal Analysis coursework)
key_responsibilities: Develop embedded software from bare metal to embedded Linux plus higher level interface software
Code in C, C++, Bash, Python on bare metal and RHEL-compatible Linux in containers
Debug software-hardware interactions using schematics, datasheets, and lab equipment (oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, DMMs, SMUs)
Cross-discipline collaboration with electrical, control, and mechanical engineers across Boise, San Jose, Penang, Hyderabad
Hands-on daily work with electronics and lab equipment to root-cause system-level issues

strengths: Register-level bare-metal peripheral programming (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1 on STM32 Cortex-M4 in the Temperature Monitor project) is genuine signal/register-level debug experience, directly backing the JD minimum qualification

Cross-discipline team leadership (General Secretary, Agnel Robotics Club) coordinated mechanical, electrical, and software work across a 25-member team on PCB fabrication and AI/ML integration end to end, which maps to the JD ask for working in cross-discipline design teams

Multiple from-scratch full-stack hardware+software builds (COFFIN capstone spanning mobile client, edge server, Jetson+Arduino, multiple sensors over I2C/UART; Object Tracking Turret with STM32+UART+PWM+ToF) show real comfort building and integrating physical systems, not just isolated firmware snippets
real_gaps: No embedded Linux firmware experience. Every embedded project is bare-metal only (STM32) or uses Jetson/Raspberry Pi purely as an application-layer host, not as a target for bring-up, BSP work, or kernel/driver level firmware. The JD explicitly wants bare metal to embedded Linux, and RHEL-compatible Linux in containers, which is unaddressed
No PCIe experience anywhere in the profile, called out as a required interface
No container experience (Docker or similar), a stated preferred qualification

Board bring-up experience is not demonstrated. PCB work is single-layer EAGLE boards for robotics club locomotive robots; that is PCB design and fabrication, not first-power-on bring-up or debugging power rails, clocks, or interfaces on a new board, which is what the JD specifically asks about

Scale and domain mismatch: the JD is for custom in-house semiconductor manufacturing equipment, industrial control systems with SMU-level electrical characterization. The profile is entirely student and internship scope (robotics club boards, capstone project, coursework), a real step down in system complexity and stakes from equipment that runs a fab line
overstated_by_keywords: Oscilloscopes and Logic Analyzers are listed in the Tools skills section but no experience bullet anywhere describes actually using either to debug a real signal or timing issue, so the keyword match counted these as Have when the depth behind them is unverified

Schematics and datasheets: counted as Have because of PCB/EAGLE design experience, but that is drawing schematics for simple robotics boards, not reading and reasoning about someone else's datasheets and timing diagrams to root-cause a hardware interaction, which is the JD framing

PCB layout review for power/clocks/interfaces: the actual PCB experience is single-layer boards for locomotive robots, not the power and clock integrity review implied by the JD preferred qualification
llm_analysis.reasoning: The keyword match looks strong because the surface vocabulary overlaps heavily (C/C++, GPIO/SPI/I2C/UART, oscilloscopes, PCB), but the JD is really asking for embedded Linux bring-up and independent hardware debug on industrial equipment, and the profile has neither embedded Linux firmware work nor board bring-up nor PCIe. The genuine strength is register-level bare-metal programming and cross-discipline systems building, which should carry real weight in an interview, but the resume should not imply Linux BSP or bring-up experience it does not have.
